Hi all — initial draft answers below. I focused on the items Globex called out; happy to expand any section for the PDF. I'm attaching a working draft (dr_response_draft.md) — call out any commercial-level caveats and I will produce the final PDF.

1) High-level architecture for multi-region resilience- Redwood runs an active primary region for customer traffic and maintains warm standby capacity in at least one geographically separated region for hosted customers. Control plane metadata (model versions, tenant config) is replicated asynchronously but with near-real-time replication using quorum writes to two regions for critical metadata. For Dedicated customers with reserved capacity we provide the option of fully cross-region active-passive mirrors or customer-managed multi-region deployments depending on contractual terms.

2) RTO / RPO- Hosted API (standard): RTO for API-level recovery (traffic re-routing + warm standby spin-up) is typically 10-20 minutes for full cutover in the event of a region outage. RPO for customer persisted data (logs, audit events, stored user assets) is under 5 minutes for critical telemetry (replicated to secondary region within 60–120s) and under 1 hour for long-term archival tiers. Note: short-lived in-memory model state (per-request KV cache, streaming contexts) is ephemeral and cannot be guaranteed during cross-region failover; we capture request metadata and have replay strategies but active chat sessions may need client-side retry logic.

- Dedicated (reserved pools): RTO SLA options available in contract (1–6 hours) based on reserved capacity and warm standby configuration. RPO for Dedicated can be configured to near-zero if using synchronous replication option (contract-level feature).

3) Failover model and traffic cutover- We use smart routing at the front-door layer (edge routers + health checks) to detect region unavailability and route to the standby region. The default pattern is warm-standby: pre-warmed VMs/containers and pre-loaded model weights to minimize cold-start. Cutover sequence: 1) detect and disable unhealthy region, 2) route new requests to standby, 3) rehydrate KV/cache as capacity allows, 4) gradual traffic ramp to avoid capacity spikes. Expected traffic cutover time is dominated by model load times but typically completes within the RTO window above. For high-availability customers we offer active-active read routing for stateless workloads.

4) Data replication and retention- Telemetry and logs: replicated to a secondary region with encryption in-transit and at-rest; retention policies configurable per customer. Customer uploads (if used) are stored in encrypted object storage with cross-region replication for hosted accounts. We maintain audit logs for 90 days in primary/secondary and longer-term archives as agreed.

5) Runbooks and incident evidence- We maintain runbook excerpts for region failover, including roles (on-call, SRE lead, routing owner), steps for traffic cutover, validation checks, and rollback criteria. We perform quarterly tabletop exercises and an annual partial failover test (warm-standby promotion) for the hosted control plane. Evidence (post-mortem summaries and test logs) can be provided under an NDA; SOC2 Type II reports cover the control environment and are available via our compliance portal.

6) Customer impact and best practices- For minimal user-visible disruption, customers should implement client-side retry/backoff for streaming sessions and design prompts to be idempotent where possible. For session continuity across regions we recommend persisting session state to our replicated storage and rehydrating on reconnection.

Limitations / items requiring discussion:
- Live per-request KV cache persistence across regions is not guaranteed; for stateful session continuity we will need a tailored design (can be part of Dedicated scope).
- Some forensic artifacts (raw disk images) are not shared; summaries/log extracts can be provided under NDA.

I will produce a polished PDF for Globex after we incorporate any legal/commercial caveats.
